what: Search results (spec/pages.md §6.13): what it is and what it sold for used, where the search looked and what each site answered, then one list across the sites. Visitors can search.
frame: Who: the hunter and the person checking a price (personas), from the Buy tab's box or a product page; a visitor from the website.
Came to do: see every copy for sale in one list and which one is the best buy delivered.
Where a mistake costs most: a cheap row that is the wrong size or not the same thing, and a site that is still answering read as 'nothing there'.
Ways out (spec/ways-out.md §6.12 to §6.17): every row opens its listing and the site; Watch this search; a visitor watches only after signing in, asked at that moment.
In the loop: nothing here acts for the person; Watch this search opens the want with every value guessed and waiting on their tap.
decisions: One list, ranked by how sure the match is, then by the delivered total: a wrong size above the right one wastes the hunter's look (spec buy.md Ranking puts the label second; this puts it first, agent proposal).

Where the search looked is a strip of five site logos with each one's count, a spinner where a site is still answering and 'None' where it answered with nothing: a sentence would hide which site is late.
The summary says the used range and the price new in one sentence in words a person says back; the range bar is kept for the listing, where there is a price to place on it.
The official option is in the summary sentence (new, and delivered) and not a row: in this data it never beats the used range, and spec says it sits beside a used one only when it wins.
Price history is one Notice with a chevron, because it leads to its own page.
Watch this search is the nav's one action (a bell), as eBay's saved search is, and the empty state's one act.
Demo states by address: ?at=slow has only one site in so far; a query with no product finds nothing.
While a site is still answering, a spinner takes the camera's place in the box, so nothing moves; the camera comes back when every site is in.
Each row's fact line says its condition before what it costs ('Like new, delivered $72.50'): rows under one product share a title, so the condition tells them apart (break-ui).
Loading is the page's skeleton, failed says what did not load with Try again, and offline keeps the last copy under 'Waiting for signal' (app/src/buy/states.tsx), the same on every buy page.
